selection: Use either of the two received flaring-kit candidates only if it includes a true 4.75 mm / 3/16 in die and makes clean 45-degree double/inverted flares
exact_spec: Must clamp and flare 4.75 mm / 3/16 in brake tube; double/inverted flare required; practice on scrap before vehicle lines
next_action: Shelf-check both flaring kits: photograph labels/dies, confirm one has a 3/16 in / 4.75 mm die, then make at least five scrap cut/deburr/double-flare samples before vehicle fabrication.

selection: Use the ordered Harden 3-22 mm mini tube cutter if it cuts 4.75 mm tube squarely
exact_spec: Clean square cuts on 4.75 mm / 3/16 in, 6 mm, and 8 mm tube without crushing
next_action: Receipt-check cutter wheel action and test on scrap tube

selection: Use the ordered internal/external tube deburrer or reamer only if receipt check proves it fits 4.75 mm / 3/16 in brake tube

selection: Use calipers and a metric thread pitch gauge to identify flare nuts and port threads
exact_spec: Must distinguish M10x1.0, M10x1.25, M12x1.0, and any non-metric fitted hardware before buying fittings
next_action: Confirm on hand before fitting purchase
reject_if: Threads are guessed from vehicle year or by eye only
notes: Do not buy flare nuts by catalog logic alone because the brake system has prior conversion history.

selection: User reports the copper-coloured hard-line tube has arrived; use it only if label/spec proves brake-rated CuNi/Cunifer 4.75 mm / 3/16 in tube or brake-rated coated steel
exact_spec: 10000 mm minimum if combining brake and clutch; 12000 mm preferred; no bare copper
next_action: Photograph the coil label/printing and measure OD before release. If it is brake-rated CuNi/Cunifer or automotive brake-rated coated 3/16 in tube, cut scrap and prove clean flares; if it is bare/plumbing copper, do not use it for final brake hydraulics.
reject_if: Bare copper, plumbing tube, refrigeration tube, used tube, unknown rating, compression tube, or stainless tube that the shop/tool cannot flare cleanly
notes: CuNi/Cunifer is preferred for in-house shaping because it is easier to bend and flare; bundy steel is acceptable if the fabricator can form clean bends and flares. User update 2026-06-18 says the copper tubing arrived, but final brake use remains blocked until the material is proven brake-rated CuNi/Cunifer or automotive brake-rated tube rather than bare/plumbing copper.

item: Rear axle tee and inline unions
